title: Lifts of exact functors to module objects are exact
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be abelian monoidal categories whose tensor products are additive in
each variable. Let $\mathcal R$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal S$ a monoid object of
$\mathcal D$ such that $\mathcal R\otimes-$ and $\mathcal S\otimes-$ are right exact, so that
$\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ and $\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal D)$ are abelian
([lem-sfb-modobj-abelian]); write $U_{\mathcal R}$, $U_{\mathcal S}$ for the forgetful functors. Let
$F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive exact functor and
$G\colon\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal D)$ a functor with
$U_{\mathcal S}\circ G=F\circ U_{\mathcal R}$. Then $G$ is additive and exact; in particular it preserves
finite limits and finite colimits.

proof.text: Use the already proved module-object API in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Mod.Abelian (the module realizing [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian]) and its public dependency Monoidal.Mod.Limits. Both forgetful functors are additive; the source forgetful functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits, and the target forgetful functor reflects finite limits and finite colimits. These are existing proved instances, not new assumptions. Their module categories and forgetful functors are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

It becomes the source forgetful functor followed by F, which is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits by composition. These are exactly the notions in [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] and [def-galois-exact-functor].

proof.text: The target forgetful functor is faithful by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-faithful]. Apply Mathlib Functor.additive_of_comp_faithful to obtain additivity of G. Apply Mathlib preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves and preservesFiniteColimits_of_reflects_of_preserves to G and the target forgetful functor, using the three composite instances from the preceding step. This gives finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation of G directly, and assembling the three proofs gives the assertion.
